cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's spent a good while on how they should run their gatherings (1 Corinthians 11-14). Now he switches gears to the BIG one: the gospel.

cards.question: The gospel Paul brings up here is brand new to the Corinthians.

cards.text: Paul is reminding them. They received this gospel, they stand firm in it, and Paul says by this gospel they are saved.

cards.question: Paul puts an "if" on it. The Corinthians are saved by this gospel if they do what?

answers.text: Hold firmly to the word he preached
Keep every feast in the law

cards.text: Otherwise, Paul says, they have believed in vain. Then he gets to what he calls "of first importance", and friend, when Paul says FIRST importance, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Before Paul lists what's of first importance, he says what he did with this message. What was it?

answers.text: He received it and passed it on
He kept it to himself for years
He wrote it down for the elders

cards.question: First thing on Paul's list: Christ died for our ___, according to the Scriptures.

cards.text: Christ died, according to the Scriptures. Then He was buried, and friend, if the list stopped THERE, this would be the saddest letter ever written.

cards.question: But Paul's list keeps going: Christ was raised. When?
Paul says Christ being raised happened according to the Scriptures, just like His death.

cards.text: Now Paul brings the receipts: the people who saw Christ after He was raised. First, He appeared to Cephas, that's Peter (John 1:42).

cards.question: After the risen Christ appears to Peter, who sees Him next on Paul's list?
Then Paul names a whole crowd. How many brothers see the risen Christ at once?
Paul says most of the brothers in that crowd are still living when he writes this letter.

cards.text: Then Christ appears to James, and then to all the apostles. And Paul's got one more name for the list.

cards.question: Last of all, the risen Christ appears to Paul, the man writing this letter.

cards.text: Paul says it happened to him "as to one of untimely birth." Then he calls himself the least of the apostles, unworthy to even be called one, and I bet there's a reason he feels that way.

cards.question: Why does Paul say he's unworthy to be called an apostle?

answers.text: He persecuted the church of God
He was the youngest of them

cards.text: Paul goes from "the least of the apostles" to "I am what I am" in one breath, friend. That's a BIG turnaround, and something got him there.

cards.question: Paul calls himself the least of the apostles. So what does he say made him what he is now?
Paul says he worked harder than all of the other apostles.

cards.text: Then Paul adds, "yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me." Friend, a worn-out stamper doesn't sharpen his own edges. Mine came back sharp, and I sure didn't do it.

cards.question: Whether it was Paul or the other apostles, this is what they ___, and this is what the Corinthians believed.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Keep that oven warm, friend, because Paul's not done with this teaching. Not even close.

findings.problem: Too many choices depend on discovery guesses rather than reasoning from earlier cards. For example, stop 1 cards 2, 7, 9 and 10, and stop 2 cards 2, 3 and 11, ask for information that the earlier cards provide no basis for inferring. Even treating the remaining choices as informed, only half of the walkthrough's choices are informed guesses, rather than most.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen wording "sins" in "Christ died for our ___." None of the earlier cards supplies a way to infer that word, so this is guessing the next word of Paul's line rather than testing meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The correct answer verifies both that Christ's raising was according to the Scriptures and that His death was according to the Scriptures. That uses verses 3 and 4, but the card cites only verse 4; it should cite 1 Corinthians 15:3-4.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower. A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The phrase "that crowd" points back to card 3, which is no longer on screen. The question does not identify the crowd within itself, such as the brothers who saw the risen Christ at once.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: James appears for the first time with only his name. Papa Dorin does not simply say who James is, as he did when introducing Paul and identifying Cephas as Peter.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The card quotes "the least of the apostles" from verse 9 and "I am what I am" from verse 10, but its citation covers only verse 10. It should cite 1 Corinthians 15:9-10.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the sentence introducing Paul's quotation, the sentence about a worn-out stamper, and the sentence about Papa Dorin's edges. It exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The closing story card has three sentences: "And that's where we'll leave it for now.", the sentence beginning "Keep that oven warm", and "Not even close." The continuation line is permitted, but it still exceeds the two-sentence limit for a non-opening story card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
